title: China-to-Uganda PPE Respirator (FFP Mask) Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Conformity Assessment — UNBS PVoC, Certificate of Conformity, and Q-Mark
rows.target_requirement: UNBS applies a mandatory conformity pathway for PPE respirators through Pre-Export Verification of Conformity and consignment-based import controls. Before release for Uganda entry, the exporter and Uganda importer must complete the PVoC process for the exact model, obtain a valid UNBS Certificate of Conformity (CoC), and demonstrate readiness for customs release via the chosen route. The Q-Mark requirement is part of UNBS quality control expectations for regulated imports, and clearance is typically processed through the Mombasa or Dar es Salaam channels for landlocked Uganda shipments.
target_standards: UNBS Conformity and Certification Guidelines (PVoC to Standards)
Uganda import control requirements for regulated PPE through UNBS
Q-Mark quality-mark guidance for selected regulated categories
rows.china_equivalent: China typically uses GB 2626-2019 and GB 19083-2010 with CNCA-administered CCC or NMPA medical-device filings at factory and product levels. These are domestic mandatory systems and are not equivalent to Uganda consignment-level UNBS PVoC and CoC requirements before Uganda release, nor to Q-Mark placement expectations.
china_standards: GB 2626-2019 — Respiratory protective equipment technical baseline in China
GB 19083-2010 — Medical-protective mask baseline in China
CCC and NMPA filing systems under Chinese supervision
rows.gap: A common gap is assuming that CNAS and CCC paperwork is sufficient for Uganda release. For Uganda entry, gap closure requires an Uganda consignment CoC, importer-linked customs routing documentation, evidence of UNBS PVoC outcome, and Q-Mark coverage where required by product category. Without this, release teams at transit channels usually block shipment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — UNBS PVoC, per-shipment Certificate of Conformity, and Q-Mark readiness documentation are required before customs release in Uganda channels.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB 2626 or GB 19083 domestic compliance and CCC/NMPA pathways apply inside China but do not by themselves meet Uganda import release requirements.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For Uganda, Chinese CNAS, CCC, or NMPA paperwork is not a replacement for UNBS consignment-level PVoC and Certificate of Conformity requirements. Exporters need importer-linked documentation and Q-Mark alignment before release through Mombasa or Dar es Salaam.

source.publisher: UNBS official portals and published certification notices

rows.requirement: Labelling and Instructions — Uganda Placement, Importer Identity, and Power/Radio Declarations
rows.target_requirement: Instructions for Uganda-bound products should provide English information matching market use, including performance class, limits, fit guidance, storage and shelf-life, cleaning or reuse position, and importer traceability. For routes where electrical ratings are declared, the statement should use Uganda-consistent 240 V and 50 Hz context. If the model includes radio communication, include UCC-related statement text required for destination review. The importer should be identifiable for release workflows through Mombasa or Dar es Salaam channels.
target_standards: UNBS/market practice for importer-linked information in regulated PPE consignments
Uganda power declaration alignment with 240 V and 50 Hz context
UCC declaration format for radio-capable product claims
EN 149 documentation content for user notices
rows.china_equivalent: China-oriented GB 2626 documentation typically uses Chinese instructions and domestic labeling structures. This is not directly reusable for Uganda market placement unless translated and routed with importer and telecom context. Domestic import files may not mention Mombasa or Dar es Salaam transit linkage.
china_standards: CNCA export filing practices for domestic circulation
rows.gap: The gap is destination language, routing traceability, and declaration alignment. Exporters should produce Uganda-ready labels and manuals, identify the Uganda importer with customs role clarity, and add power and UCC notes in the relevant product variants. A CN-only manual with incomplete route context is a frequent clearance issue.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — Uganda-ready instructions, importer traceability, and route-specific declarations (including power and UCC notes where relevant) are required before market placement.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — Chinese market labelling under GB 2626 remains mandatory domestically and is separate from Uganda release documents.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Uganda placement files require market-language documentation, importer traceability, and destination declarations for electrical and radio-related claims. CN-only labels and generic manuals are usually insufficient for release.

source.publisher: UNBS and Uganda trade logistics disclosures

rows.requirement: Marking — EN 149 Identity and UNBS Q-Mark Visibility
rows.target_requirement: For Uganda, EN 149-aligned models must carry marking that clearly identifies class, model, manufacturer, and tested route. Q-Mark presentation is expected where the product falls under UNBS quality-traceability expectation. If the model includes powered or radio functions, mark declarations must align with Uganda import declarations including 240 V and 50 Hz references where applicable.
target_standards: UNBS product marking interpretation for EN 149-based respirator imports
UNBS Q-Mark visibility expectations for regulated commodities
Product declaration consistency for power and accessory statements
rows.china_equivalent: GB 2626 product marking and Chinese domestic marking language are typically CN-focused, with KN terminology and domestic traceability fields. CCC mark presence supports domestic entry but does not provide the Uganda-facing mark layer required for Q-Mark and UNBS route documents.
china_standards: China CCC mark and traceability practice
rows.gap: The key marking gap is market-fit conversion. Exporters should replace CN-only KN markings with Uganda EN 149 model-identifiers in the filing model, display route-aligned quality symbols such as UNBS Q-Mark when required, and keep power/radio-related marking consistent with Uganda declarations.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — market-accurate EN 149 model marking and UNBS quality symbol alignment are required for accepted import documentation
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB 2626 marking and CCC mark are mandatory for domestic Chinese market flows where applicable.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Uganda-facing marking must match the UNBS-adopted EN 149 model route and include route-appropriate quality visibility such as UNBS Q-Mark. CN-only KN labels and domestic-only traceability marks are generally insufficient.

rows.requirement: Filtering Respirator Safety — UNBS Adoption of EN 149 (FFP1/FFP2/FFP3)
rows.target_requirement: UNBS technical baseline for respirators is built on EN 149 class-based performance with KN and medical pathways treated separately. For occupational filtering respirators, classes FFP1, FFP2 and FFP3 apply and test evidence is expected for aerosol efficiency, breathing resistance, inward leakage behaviour, carbon dioxide content, and clogging/handling characteristics under practical use assumptions. Uganda market files often note that US standards references and IEC-based test practice can be used for technical interoperability, especially for accessories and measurement equipment context.
target_standards: UNBS-adopted EN 149 technical framework for filtering facepiece respirators
US and IEC-referenced test-method references used for compatibility context
rows.china_equivalent: China relies on GB 2626-2019 for industrial respirators, with KN90 and KN95 classes and CNAS laboratory testing patterns. GB 2626 is a domestic baseline and is useful for preliminary screening, but differences in method breadth and destination documentation make it insufficient as standalone Uganda safety evidence.
china_standards: CNAS testing framework under Chinese market oversight
rows.gap: The practical gap is not only nominal class mapping. Uganda-facing technical files should include EN 149 test scope evidence aligned to the exact marketed model and any accessory variant. A KN95 laboratory report alone is not sufficient for Uganda occupational release where EN 149 pathway validation is requested.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — EN 149 class evidence and model-matched technical dossier are required for occupational UNBS route documents
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB 2626 compliance records are mandatory for the China domestic market, but are not the sole Uganda route evidence.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Uganda requires EN 149 class-consistent occupational respiratory evidence for workplace models. GB 2626 KN-level documentation supports domestic screening only and should not be treated as direct Uganda acceptance evidence unless adapted to the UNBS route.

source.publisher: UNBS technical publications and related laboratory guidance

rows.requirement: Medical-Protective Masks and Radio-Capable Accessories — Separate Health and UCC Controls
rows.target_requirement: Masks positioned for clinical protection, infection control, or surgical-like use are not treated as occupational respirators in Uganda. They follow the national health regulator route, with separate documentation for intended medical use. For models including radio modules, the radio function is reviewed under Uganda Communications Commission expectations, and safety declaration should mention compatibility with Uganda electricity context only where applicable.
target_standards: National health authority route for medical masks in Uganda
Uganda Communications Commission regulation framework for radio-capable devices
UNBS occupational respirator standard pathway excludes clinical-use models
rows.china_equivalent: GB 19083-2010 is China’s medical-protective baseline and is processed under NMPA medical pathways. This is not a direct substitute for Uganda health-regulator routing. Accessory-led radio declarations are not resolved through GB 19083 alone and require destination-specific telecom interpretation.
china_standards: UCC telecom-related declarations where radio or wireless modules are present
rows.gap: Using one compliance file for both workplace respirator and medical claims is the highest-risk gap pattern. Uganda expects clean route separation and evidence that radio-capable claims are reviewed under telecom expectations. Exporters should avoid mixed-language routing and submit destination-specific documentation per model.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — route separation between workplace respirator and medical products; radio-capable models need UCC-aligned declarations as applicable
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB 19083 and related NMPA documentation are mandatory in China for medical-protective products but do not replace Uganda healthcare or UCC routing.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Medical or surgical claims must not be run as occupational EN 149 imports only. Medical route and telecom-function checks must be treated separately in Uganda destination documentation.

source.publisher: Uganda Communications Commission and Uganda health sector notices

rows.requirement: Scope and Intended-Use Classification — Occupational Respirator vs Medical Mask Route
rows.target_requirement: Uganda applies use-based classification for this product type. Workplace filtering respirators with particulate protection claims are processed through UNBS technical routes adopting EN 149 classes FFP1, FFP2, and FFP3. Medical masks or surgical-use products are processed through the national health regulator route instead of the workplace respirator EN 149 path. If the model includes radio communication functions, regulatory review of telecom aspects is done under the UCC framework, while power accessories must match Uganda declaration context (240 V, 50 Hz).
target_standards: UNBS product classification under workplace PPE framework and Ministry of Gender and Labour directives
National health regulator pathway for medical and surgical masks
Uganda Communications Commission (UCC) rules for radio-capable products
UNBS adoption of EN 149 classes (FFP1, FFP2, FFP3)
rows.china_equivalent: China separates industrial respiratory products under GB 2626 and medical-protective masks under GB 19083 with corresponding certification tracks. This domestic split is structurally similar but does not determine Uganda scope automatically; Uganda depends on UNBS occupational classification and national health authority decisions for destination market placement.
rows.gap: The biggest gap is route selection before shipment. A model labelled for workplace wearer protection must be aligned to UNBS occupational evidence and EN 149 classes. Any clinical or surgical claims move the model to health-regulator controls. Wireless or radio claims add a separate UCC review, and incomplete routing declarations are common causes of return to shipper.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — destination-market classification by intended use must be documented and cannot mix occupational and medical routes without route-specific evidence.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB 2626 and GB 19083 represent the two domestic Chinese routes but do not by themselves define Uganda destination scope.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Uganda’s import route is use-dependent: occupational respirators follow UNBS occupational conformity and EN 149 class rules, while medical-mask claims follow the health regulator route, and radio features trigger UCC considerations.

source.publisher: UNBS and Uganda Ministry of Health/Ministry of Gender and Labour public notices
